key_terms.مَا خَرَجَ مِنْهُ: What comes out from it (the yield/profit)

ai.seo_question: What are the financial obligations of a seller regarding maintenance and yield when selling green plants before harvest?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the risk allocation in sales of unharvested crops, specifying that the seller retains liability for maintenance costs (tasq) and expenses (nafaqa) while keeping the right to the yield. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that ownership entails bearing the associated burdens until the transfer of risk is complete, ensuring fairness in agricultural transactions. It serves as a practical application of the general contract law principles found in Usul al-Kafi regarding conditional sales.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama’at,
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

similar to it, and there is an increase in it, ‘(He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘So if he were to do it, upon him would be its maintenance and its expenditure, and for him would be whatever comes out from it’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from abu Ayyub from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “Sama‘ah has narrated a similar Hadith from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, with this addition, ‘
If he leaves it until ears appear, he is responsible for its maintenance and expenses and he can have whatever comes out thereof.”’
